title: "Pesah, Freedom in Individuality" SCA Pesah Message by Mrs. Danielle Hazan

chapters.title: The names of Pesah
chapters.about: Exploring the various names of Pesah and why it is primarily called Pesah.

chapters.title: The symbol of the sheep
chapters.about: Examining sheep as a symbol of passive behavior and following the crowd.

chapters.title: Freedom through individuality
chapters.about: Connecting the Korban Pesah to the requirement of thinking for oneself to be free.

claims: "A passage from an article states..." - The teacher quotes an article about 400 sheep in 2006 in Turkey, which is background knowledge added by the teacher not inherent to the Torah concept of the Korban Pesach.
summary: Mrs. Hazan discusses why the holiday of Pesah is primarily named after the Korban Pesah rather than other names like Chag Ha'Aviv or Z'man Cheiruteinu. She explains that sacrificing the sheep symbolized rejecting passive follower behavior in order to achieve true freedom through individuality.
questions: Why is the holiday most commonly called Pesah instead of its other names?
What does the Korban Pesah symbolize regarding freedom?
How do the characteristics of sheep relate to passive behavior?
What is required in order to be truly free?
